scene.label: Act 3, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. A room in Ford's house

content.text: Enter Mistress Ford and Mistress Page.

lines.text: What, John! What, Robert!
lines.plainText: What John What Robert

lines.text: Quickly, quickly! Is the buck-basket—

lines.text: I warrant.—What, Robin, I say!

content.text: Enter John and Robert with a great buck-basket.

lines.text: Come, come, come.
lines.plainText: Come come come

lines.text: Here, set it down.
lines.plainText: Here set it down

lines.text: Give your men the charge; we must be brief.
lines.plainText: Give your men the charge we must be brief

lines.text: Marry, as I told you before, John and Robert, be ready here hard by in the brew-house; and when I suddenly call you, come forth, and, without any pause or staggering, take this basket on your shoulders. That done, trudge with it in all haste, and carry it among the whitsters in Datchet Mead, and there empty it in the muddy ditch close by the Thames side.

lines.text: You will do it?
lines.plainText: You will do it

lines.text: I ha' told them over and over, they lack no direction.—Be gone, and come when you are called.

lines.text: How now, my eyas-musket, what news with you?
lines.plainText: How now my eyasmusket what news with you

lines.text: My Master, Sir John, is come in at your back door, Mistress Ford, and requests your company.
lines.plainText: My Master Sir John is come in at your back door Mistress Ford and requests your company

lines.text: You little Jack-a-Lent, have you been true to us?
lines.plainText: You little JackaLent have you been true to us

lines.text: Ay, I'll be sworn. My master knows not of your being here, and hath threatened to put me into everlasting liberty if I tell you of it; for he swears he'll turn me away.
lines.plainText: Ay I'll be sworn My master knows not of your being here and hath threatened to put me into everlasting liberty if I tell you of it for he swears he'll turn me away

lines.text: Thou'rt a good boy, this secrecy of thine shall be a tailor to thee, and shall make thee a new doublet and hose. I'll go hide me.
lines.plainText: Thou'rt a good boy this secrecy of thine shall be a tailor to thee and shall make thee a new doublet and hose I'll go hide me

lines.text: Do so.—Go tell thy master I am alone.
lines.plainText: Do soGo tell thy master I am alone

lines.text: I warrant thee. If I do not act it, hiss me.
lines.plainText: I warrant thee If I do not act it hiss me

lines.text: Go to, then. We'll use this unwholesome humidity, this gross watery pumpion; we'll teach him to know turtles from jays.
lines.plainText: Go to then We'll use this unwholesome humidity this gross watery pumpion we'll teach him to know turtles from jays

lines.text: "Have I caught thee, my heavenly jewel?" Why, now let me die, for I have lived long enough. This is the period of my ambition. O this blessed hour!
lines.plainText: Have I caught thee my heavenly jewel Why now let me die for I have lived long enough This is the period of my ambition O this blessed hour

lines.text: O, sweet Sir John!
lines.plainText: O sweet Sir John

lines.text: Mistress Ford, I cannot cog, I cannot prate, Mistress Ford. Now shall I sin in my wish: I would thy husband were dead. I'll speak it before the best lord: I would make thee my lady.
lines.plainText: Mistress Ford I cannot cog I cannot prate Mistress Ford Now shall I sin in my wish I would thy husband were dead I'll speak it before the best lord I would make thee my lady

lines.text: I your lady, Sir John? Alas, I should be a pitiful lady.
lines.plainText: I your lady Sir John Alas I should be a pitiful lady

lines.text: Let the court of France show me such another. I see how thine eye would emulate the diamond. Thou hast the right arched beauty of the brow that becomes the ship-tire, the tire-valiant, or any tire of Venetian admittance.
lines.plainText: Let the court of France show me such another I see how thine eye would emulate the diamond Thou hast the right arched beauty of the brow that becomes the shiptire the tirevaliant or any tire of Venetian admittance

lines.text: A plain kerchief, Sir John. My brows become nothing else, nor that well neither.
lines.plainText: A plain kerchief Sir John My brows become nothing else nor that well neither

lines.text: By the Lord, thou art a traitor to say so. Thou wouldst make an absolute courtier, and the firm fixture of thy foot would give an excellent motion to thy gait in a semi-circled farthingale. I see what thou wert, if Fortune thy foe were not, Nature thy friend. Come, thou canst not hide it.
lines.plainText: By the Lord thou art a traitor to say so Thou wouldst make an absolute courtier and the firm fixture of thy foot would give an excellent motion to thy gait in a semicircled farthingale I see what thou wert if Fortune thy foe were not Nature thy friend Come thou canst not hide it

lines.text: Believe me, there's no such thing in me.
lines.plainText: Believe me there's no such thing in me

lines.text: What made me love thee? Let that persuade thee there's something extraordinary in thee. Come, I cannot cog and say thou art this and that, like a many of these lisping hawthorn buds that come like women in men's apparel, and smell like Bucklersbury in simple-time. I cannot. But I love thee, none but thee; and thou deservest it.
lines.plainText: What made me love thee Let that persuade thee there's something extraordinary in thee Come I cannot cog and say thou art this and that like a many of these lisping hawthorn buds that come like women in men's apparel and smell like Bucklersbury in simpletime I cannot But I love thee none but thee and thou deservest it

lines.text: Do not betray me, sir; I fear you love Mistress Page.
lines.plainText: Do not betray me sir I fear you love Mistress Page

lines.text: Thou mightst as well say I love to walk by the Counter gate, which is as hateful to me as the reek of a lime-kiln.
lines.plainText: Thou mightst as well say I love to walk by the Counter gate which is as hateful to me as the reek of a limekiln

lines.text: Well, heaven knows how I love you, and you shall one day find it.
lines.plainText: Well heaven knows how I love you and you shall one day find it

lines.text: Keep in that mind, I'll deserve it.
lines.plainText: Keep in that mind I'll deserve it

lines.text: Nay, I must tell you, so you do; or else I could not be in that mind.
lines.plainText: Nay I must tell you so you do or else I could not be in that mind

lines.text: Mistress Ford, Mistress Ford, here's Mistress Page at the door, sweating and blowing and looking wildly, and would needs speak with you presently.
lines.plainText: Mistress Ford Mistress Ford here's Mistress Page at the door sweating and blowing and looking wildly and would needs speak with you presently

lines.text: She shall not see me; I will ensconce me behind the arras.
lines.plainText: She shall not see me I will ensconce me behind the arras

lines.text: Pray you, do so; she's a very tattling woman.
lines.plainText: Pray you do so she's a very tattling woman

lines.text: O Mistress Ford, what have you done? You're shamed, you're overthrown, you're undone for ever!
lines.plainText: O Mistress Ford what have you done You're shamed you're overthrown you're undone for ever

lines.text: What's the matter, good Mistress Page?
lines.plainText: What's the matter good Mistress Page

lines.text: O well-a-day, Mistress Ford, having an honest man to your husband, to give him such cause of suspicion!
lines.plainText: O welladay Mistress Ford having an honest man to your husband to give him such cause of suspicion

lines.text: What cause of suspicion?
lines.plainText: What cause of suspicion

lines.text: What cause of suspicion? Out upon you! How am I mistook in you!

lines.text: Why, alas, what's the matter?
lines.plainText: Why alas what's the matter

lines.text: Your husband's coming hither, woman, with all the officers in Windsor, to search for a gentleman that he says is here now in the house, by your consent, to take an ill advantage of his absence. You are undone.
lines.plainText: Your husband's coming hither woman with all the officers in Windsor to search for a gentleman that he says is here now in the house by your consent to take an ill advantage of his absence You are undone

lines.text: 'Tis not so, I hope.
lines.plainText: 'Tis not so I hope

lines.text: Pray heaven it be not so, that you have such a man here! But 'tis most certain your husband's coming, with half Windsor at his heels, to search for such a one. I come before to tell you. If you know yourself clear, why, I am glad of it; but if you have a friend here, convey, convey him out. Be not amazed, call all your senses to you; defend your reputation, or bid farewell to your good life for ever.
lines.plainText: Pray heaven it be not so that you have such a man here But 'tis most certain your husband's coming with half Windsor at his heels to search for such a one I come before to tell you If you know yourself clear why I am glad of it but if you have a friend here convey convey him out Be not amazed call all your senses to you defend your reputation or bid farewell to your good life for ever

lines.text: What shall I do? There is a gentleman, my dear friend; and I fear not mine own shame as much as his peril. I had rather than a thousand pound he were out of the house.
lines.plainText: What shall I do There is a gentleman my dear friend and I fear not mine own shame as much as his peril I had rather than a thousand pound he were out of the house

lines.text: For shame! Never stand "you had rather" and "you had rather". Your husband's here at hand. Bethink you of some conveyance. In the house you cannot hide him. O, how have you deceived me! Look, here is a basket. If he be of any reasonable stature, he may creep in here; and throw foul linen upon him, as if it were going to bucking. Or—it is whiting-time—send him by your two men to Datchet Mead.

lines.text: [Comes out of hiding.] Let me see 't, let me see 't! O, let me see 't! I'll in, I'll in. Follow your friend's counsel. I'll in.

lines.text: What, Sir John Falstaff? Are these your letters, knight?

lines.text: I love thee, and none but thee. Help me away. Let me creep in here. I'll never—
lines.plainText: I love thee and none but thee Help me away Let me creep in here I'll never

content.text: [He goes into the basket; they cover him with dirty clothes.]

lines.text: Help to cover your master, boy.—Call your men, Mistress Ford.—You dissembling knight!

lines.text: What, John! Robert! John!

content.text: Enter Ford, Page, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.text: Pray you come near. If I suspect without cause, why then make sport at me, then let me be your jest; I deserve it.—How now? Whither bear you this?

lines.text: Why, what have you to do whither they bear it? You were best meddle with buck-washing!
lines.plainText: Why what have you to do whither they bear it You were best meddle with buckwashing

lines.text: Buck? I would I could wash myself of the buck! Buck, buck, buck! Ay, buck! I warrant you, buck, and of the season too, it shall appear.
lines.plainText: Buck I would I could wash myself of the buck Buck buck buck Ay buck I warrant you buck and of the season too it shall appear

content.text: [Exeunt John and Robert with the basket.]

lines.text: Good Master Ford, be contented: you wrong yourself too much.
lines.plainText: Good Master Ford be contented you wrong yourself too much

lines.text: True, Master Page.—Up, gentlemen, you shall see sport anon. Follow me, gentlemen.
lines.plainText: True Master PageUp gentlemen you shall see sport anon Follow me gentlemen

lines.text: This is fery fantastical humours and jealousies.
lines.plainText: This is fery fantastical humours and jealousies

lines.text: By gar, 'tis no the fashion of France; it is not jealous in France.
lines.plainText: By gar 'tis no the fashion of France it is not jealous in France

lines.text: Nay, follow him, gentlemen; see the issue of his search.
lines.plainText: Nay follow him gentlemen see the issue of his search

lines.text: Is there not a double excellency in this?
lines.plainText: Is there not a double excellency in this

lines.text: I know not which pleases me better, that my husband is deceived, or Sir John.
lines.plainText: I know not which pleases me better that my husband is deceived or Sir John

lines.text: What a taking was he in when your husband asked who was in the basket!
lines.plainText: What a taking was he in when your husband asked who was in the basket

lines.text: I am half afraid he will have need of washing, so throwing him into the water will do him a benefit.
lines.plainText: I am half afraid he will have need of washing so throwing him into the water will do him a benefit

lines.text: Hang him, dishonest rascal! I would all of the same strain were in the same distress.
lines.plainText: Hang him dishonest rascal I would all of the same strain were in the same distress

lines.text: I think my husband hath some special suspicion of Falstaff's being here, for I never saw him so gross in his jealousy till now.
lines.plainText: I think my husband hath some special suspicion of Falstaff's being here for I never saw him so gross in his jealousy till now

lines.text: I will lay a plot to try that, and we will yet have more tricks with Falstaff. His dissolute disease will scarce obey this medicine.
lines.plainText: I will lay a plot to try that and we will yet have more tricks with Falstaff His dissolute disease will scarce obey this medicine

lines.text: Shall we send that foolish carrion Mistress Quickly to him, and excuse his throwing into the water, and give him another hope, to betray him to another punishment?
lines.plainText: Shall we send that foolish carrion Mistress Quickly to him and excuse his throwing into the water and give him another hope to betray him to another punishment

lines.text: We will do it. Let him be sent for tomorrow eight o'clock to have amends.
lines.plainText: We will do it Let him be sent for tomorrow eight o'clock to have amends

lines.text: You use me well, Master Ford, do you?

lines.text: Ay, I do so.

lines.text: Heaven make you better than your thoughts!
lines.plainText: Heaven make you better than your thoughts

lines.text: Amen!

lines.text: Ay, ay; I must bear it.

lines.text: If there be anypody in the house, and in the chambers, and in the coffers, and in the presses, heaven forgive my sins at the day of judgment!

lines.text: Well, I promised you a dinner. Come, come, walk in the park. I pray you pardon me; I will hereafter make known to you why I have done this. Come, wife, come, Mistress Page, I pray you pardon me. Pray heartily, pardon me.

lines.text: Let's go in, gentlemen; but, trust me, we'll mock him. I do invite you tomorrow morning to my house to breakfast; after, we'll a-birding together; I have a fine hawk for the bush. Shall it be so?
